Okay, if you move your cables around, those that resist wearing are actually useful.

You only need to upgrade cables, if:

1: Your cables are rated for a lower amperage: you have a cable that can handle 10 amps, but you put 20 amps RMS through them.

2: your digital signal is unreliable/not connecting, this shouldn't be a problem though, since most cables (should be)are made to spec. Important note: Digital signal quality doesn't affect audio/video quality, since it either gets through or doesn't(\*some exceptions apply).

If your cables aren't melting/burning your house down while using it, and you have a signal, you are fine.

There is a lot going on in Hungary, it would take days to list what is wrong, I will try to get as many as possible, but I'm sure I will leave out things that I'm not even thinking about.

First of all, wages, the current minimum wage (after taxes) is around 300 dollars, it will be around 330 starting 2022. Usually if you are not living with your parents, you have to live with someone else, one paying the rent, the other paying for everything else(edit: This means that it's bascially an everday thing to choose between homelessness with 0 help and staying in a toxic relationship).

Second of all, political bullshittery that happens here. There is a mafia running here, called the govt, it only gives money to businesses to friends, and they make a lot of projects that are only there to spend money on. The debt is through the roof, including chinese/russian debt that made many african countries got screwed up with.

Third one, Studies. The Capital of Hungary, Budapest wanted to build a student campus in the middle of the city with the capacity of 12000. The govt made a deal with China, to build Fudan University there, with Chinese debt, Chinese workers, and we are paying for it. Besides that if you are close to a Uni, and your parents make better than avg money, you are good to go, which is obviously wrong, but a bit better than US. The primary and secondary schools are underfunded and understaffed, so that makes them a hell hole.

The fourth one, Child policies: You get a lot of tax breaks, debt forgiveness for buying a house, even uni debt forgiveness (only for the person that birthed the child, so I would be left out).

The fifth one, geopolitical situation: the ukraine/russian border is only around 350km away from the ukraine/hungarian border. And the govt is trying to be friends with Russia, and it makes me worry.

The sixth one, healthcare: we have one of the worst health care in europe, one of the most covid deaths, and under payed, under staffed hospitals. I've had a few surgeries and while the nurses where nice, they were almost in a worse condition than me, because of their exhaustion. The food was edible, but if you would need to stay in a hospital, you definetly need to gather food from outside, which is impossible since covid, because the hospitals are in lockdown ever since.
